geometry.locator: arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 1 (planes 8 m edge to edge; supermodules 14.78 m and 14.10 m; 1.15 m gap) and Sec. 6.5 (midpoint coordinate, 15.631 m, azimuth 333.4452°)
geometry.note: Derived from a surveyed point, a surveyed azimuth and published dimensions; every input is quoted in method. No independent figure measures the footprint itself, so there is no checks[] row.
geometry.quote: The far detector and cavern axes are level and at an azimuth of 333.4452° (26.5548° west of true north).

method: Derived: a rectangle in plan, 8 m wide (the 'edge to edge dimension of 8 m' of the octagonal steel planes) and 30.31 m long, centred on the surveyed midpoint of the two supermodules (47.820267 N, 92.241412 W) and aligned with the published detector and cavern axis, azimuth 333.4452° (26.5548° west of true north). Along the axis it runs from 15.631 m upstream of the midpoint ('The origin of the detector coordinate system is the upstream edge of the far detector. This lies 15.631 m upstream from the midpoint') to 14.675 m downstream (half of the 1.15 m gap plus the 14.10 m second supermodule); the first supermodule is 14.78 m long. Computed on a local equirectangular plane. Inputs are all from arXiv:0805.3170 Secs. 1, 6.5 (survey precision 0.7 m per coordinate, axis 15 microradians); accuracy_m 3 m also covers the steel-envelope definition. The coil ends, cosmic-ray veto shield and walkways are not included; this is the steel-and-scintillator stack, not the cavern.
name: MINOS far detector steel-plane envelope (plan view, derived from the published survey)
notes: The cavern (hall) is not drawn: the paper gives only the detector/cavern axis azimuth, not the cavern's size or its offset from the detector midpoint.

summary.plain: The 5,400-tonne MINOS far detector as it lies in its cavern on the 27th level: a block 8 m wide and about 30 m long, pointing along the published axis (north-north-west) toward Fermilab.
